31fbe528c34ffeff: PARIS: Zinedine Zidane's debut as France coach was overshadowed by an injury to captain Kylian Mbappe in a 1-0 win away to Turkiye on Friday, while Roberto Mancini's first game back in charge of Italy ended in a 2-0 defeat to Belgium.

Zidane, the France legend and member of the team that won the World Cup in 1998, was taking charge of Les Bleus for the first time since being appointed in late July as the successor to Didier Deschamps.
Mbappe gave his side the lead nine minutes into the second half in the UEFA Nations League Group A1 clash at the Kocaeli Stadium in Izmit, just over 100 kilometres outside Istanbul.
But the Real Madrid superstar injured himself in the process of shooting, and looked to be in clear pain when he came off a few minutes later after initially attempting to carry on.

"It's not great. Unfortunately I think he's going to have to go home. We don't want to take any risks," Zidane told broadcaster TF1, suggesting that France's all-time record goal-scorer will play no part in the three Nations League matches still to come over the next 10 days.
"He overextended his knee while shooting. It's not very encouraging."

France held on for the win without their captain, while Turkiye finished the game with 10 men after goalkeeper Ugurcan Cakir was sent off late on for handling the ball outside his box as he raced out to deny Bradley Barcola.
So it looks set to be without Mbappe that France will head to Brussels for their next game against Belgium on Monday.

Belgium, playing their first match since losing to eventual winners Spain in the World Cup quarter-finals, spoiled Mancini's return to the Italian national team by beating their hosts at the Stadio Olimpico in Rome.
Mika Godts of Paris Saint-Germain ran through to give Belgium a 20th-minute lead, and substitute Dodi Lukebakio fired in from outside the box to double their advantage after the break.
- ISAK, GYOKERES STRIKE FOR SWEDEN -

"We need to think positively and not keep banging on all the time about what has happened in the past," Mancini said later when asked if Italy's failure to qualify for the World Cup was still hanging over the nation.
"In any case we can't change what happened now," added Mancini, who also said that boos by the home fans in the crowd of almost 50,000 were "normal" and "part of the game."
Mancini was previously Italy coach between 2018 and 2023 and led them to victory at Euro 2020.
Elsewhere on Friday, Shea Charles of Fulham scored the winner deep in stoppage time as Northern Ireland won 1-0 away to Georgia in Group B2.
That was after PSG star Khvicha Kvaratskhelia had a penalty saved for the home side.
Danylo Sikan's goal gave Ukraine a 1-0 victory in Hungary in the same group, with the visitors holding on after having Oleksandr Nazarenko sent off late on.

Robert Lewandowski captained Poland in their 0-0 draw with Bosnia and Herzegovina in Group B4, while Alexander Isak and Viktor Gyokeres both scored as Sweden beat Romania 2-1 in Stockholm in the same section.
There were also wins for Armenia and Montenegro in League C.
The Nations League action continues on Saturday with England hosting Spain, who are playing their first game since winning the World Cup in July.--AFP

6ce6975d044fe723: LONDON: Former Manchester City midfielder Rodri backed the club to ultimately win a legal battle with the Premier League despite reports on Friday that the English giants have been found guilty on 114 charges.
The ruling has not yet been published and no sanctions decided.
However, the news has already sent shockwaves through English football with speculation over whether City could be relegated via a severe points deduction or have previous titles stripped.
The club are accused of breaking regulations by failing to provide accurate information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules.
However, City were also initially found guilty by Uefa in 2020 of breaking financial fair play rules and given a two-year European ban before winning an appeal at the Court of Arbitration for Sport.
"We went through an identical process in 2020," Rodri said at a press conference ahead of Spain's Nations League clash against England on Saturday.

"The club always reassured us that we would be cleared of wrongdoing, that we would face no penalties - because nothing improper had been done. We trusted the club, and ultimately, the club was acquitted."
Rodri scored the winning goal when City won their only Champions League title in 2023, among 12 major trophies with the club.
"I have faith that the club, which I know very well, will be cleared, given the reassurance they gave us back then that they had done everything by the book."
Rodri's final two seasons at City were hampered by injuries, but he was back to his best at the World Cup to lead Spain to glory.
La Roja's victory at Euro 2024 saw Rodri claim the Ballon d'Or that year and he is again among the candidates to be named the world's best player.
Unlike some of the other contenders such as Kylian Mbappe and international team-mate Lamine Yamal, he does not believe in the need to openly promote his case for the award.
"Do you think I don't want to win it? I know it’s an award that doesn't depend on what you say publicly. It depends on what you’ve shown on the pitch," said the 30-year-old.
"Individual titles are a reward for collective effort...nothing players like me have achieved makes sense without teammates."
Despite winning two major tournaments in two years, Rodri insisted Spain "are hungry for more" as they begin their Nations League campaign in front of 90,000 at Wembley.
"We are motivated to win another title," he said.
26c3af8439861c7f: A US appeals court today approved the Trump administration's blacklisting of Anthropic technology. Judges decided the US had authority to blacklist Anthropic for withholding certain AI features even if Anthropic had no malicious intent.

In a 2-1 ruling issued by the US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit, a panel of judges said the "case raises profoundly difficult questions about the appropriate military uses of an almost unimaginably powerful new technology." The US "raises the deeply sobering prospect of overly constrained AI models shutting down unexpectedly and thus causing important military operations to fail. Anthropic raises the deeply sobering prospect of unconstrained AI models hallucinating inappropriate targets for lethal military force," the ruling said.

Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "must determine how best to balance the competing risks," the court said. "In doing so here, the Secretary did not transgress any limits on his authority under the Supply Chain Security Act or the Constitution. Accordingly, we deny the petitions for review." The same court previously denied Anthropic's emergency motion for a stay in April.
8def03bc478be026: LONDON: British prime minister Andy Burnham on Friday acknowledged asylum seekers reaching the UK from France were "changing their tactics" after hundreds of people arrived on small boats this week.
A total of 781 people arrived in Britain on Wednesday after crossing the Channel on small boats - a daily record for 2026 - although numbers remain below previous years.
"They are changing their tactics but we will be relentless in chasing them down," Burnham told BBC South East of the smugglers organising the perilous crossings.
In response to a crackdown from British and French authorities, asylum seekers have sought new routes to cross the Channel, prompting multiple protests in southern England in recent weeks.

Prominent far-right activist Daniel Thomas, known as Danny Tommo, has spearheaded protests with hundreds dressed in black clothing and face coverings attempting to block the entry of migrants at various ports.
Thomas was charged for criminal damage Thursday linked to the alleged slashing of a dinghy in the Channel earlier this week.
"I recognise the concern that many people in the public have around immigration. But this is something different," Burnham told the local ITV channel in southeast England.
"That's not the British way, as far as I'm concerned," the Labour leader said of the protesters who were clad in black and sometimes masked.

Successive governments have grappled with how to curb the crossings, a lightning rod issue in the UK, where the hard-right Reform UK party has surged in popularity on the back of growing anti-immigration sentiment.
Some 18,609 people have crossed the Channel from France so far in 2026, down 42% year-on-year.
Burnham, who became prime minister in July after Keir Starmer resigned over a series of missteps, said the measures taken by his predecessor to curb irregular migration "are working".
However, he acknowledged that a "loss of collaboration with neighbours" since Britain's acrimonious exit from the European Union in 2020 had worsened the situation.
"I do point to the loss of collaboration with neighbours that came with Brexit. That hasn't helped," said Burnham.
"We don't want to see any crossings at all," said Burnham, declining to give a date for ending small boat crossings.

The Labour party will hold its first annual conference with Burnham at the helm from Sunday, where the party, buoyed by optimistic polls, will be looking for more concrete policy outlines from its new leader.

e3aa7d4c7b1120c7: When MIT mechanical engineering student Daphne Wang arrived for her internship at the Muscogee Creek Nation Department of Health in Tulsa, Oklahoma last summer, she expected to be writing code. To her surprise, she found herself analyzing tribal history and the implications for technical innovation.  “I learned so much that I think should be required curriculum for every single person in this country,” says Wang. “I think tech for good is genuinely getting out into communities and learning about people who aren't you, creating worldly perspectives that you ultimately can take into everything else that you do.” Wang and fellow intern Lucy Sun, who is majoring in artificial intelligence and decision making, spent the summer supporting the development of the Muscogee Nation's first Pregnancy Risk Assessment Monitoring System (PRAMS) survey to capture maternal health data specific to Muscogee women. The project required completing literature reviews, analyzing datasets, and drafting survey questions, while considering issues of data sovereignty and governance structures specific to the Muscogee. “It was this change of pace — 180 [degrees] from MIT, completely,” Wang reflects. At MIT, she says, course instructors routinely prepare students for big technical challenges, but there are fewer opportunities to “work with communities, [learn] how to think about the cultural and historical dimensions of the work, or how to consider the people who will be affected.”  Wang’s supervisor, epidemiologist Breanna McNaughton-Long, was effusive about Wang and Sun’s engagement. “They were instrumental. They did so much work that I don't think we would have been able to do as quickly,” she says. “And they brought this sense that we were doing something that mattered.” Experiential learning at the confluence of humanities and engineering  Wang was one of 10 MIT undergraduates to participate in the PKG Center for Social Impact’s 2026 Code.Tulsa program. Now in its second year, Code.Tulsa is made possible by support from the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation and the George Kaiser Family Foundation.  Students live at the University of Tulsa for the summer. They intern with the Muscogee and Cherokee nations, as well as local nonprofits Black Tech Street and Urban Coders Guild, completing AI, data science, and other technical projects.  The PKG Center’s assistant dean for community-based programs, Vippy Yee, complements students’ professional experience with education on the historical and cultural significance of tech-based development in the Tulsa region from the perspective of local leaders.  “As with all PKG Center programming, our aim is to help students integrate an engineer’s approach to problem-solving with a humanist lens on the nature of social challenges, and by extension interventions,” says Alison Badgett, the PKG Center’s director.  “Getting to speak to people who were either very educated on the issues or have experienced them has been a massive help in reshaping the way that I think about social issues,” says Chenise Harper, an electrical engineering with computing major who interned with the Urban Coders Guild.  Harper puts this dynamic candidly: “I hated history, but I learned a lot about why it is useful for making social change and how to go about researching it. I now feel a lot more confident that I can make an impact.” A student’s vision for increasing STEM access Code.Tulsa was the brainchild of sophomore Jack Carson, an electrical engineering and computer science (EECS) student who approached the PKG Center with the idea for Code.Tulsa as an incoming first-year student. Carson, who is from Tulsa and a member of the Cherokee Nation, saw firsthand that rural Native students who could benefit greatly from STEM education were unlikely to have access to it. Carson proposed developing a weeklong STEM camp for members of federally recognized tribes held at the University of Tulsa, with he and Code.Tulsa interns serving as instructors.  Carson devised a nomination system to attract promising high school students, selecting 25 campers from 10 tribes out of 160 applications representing 25 Native nations.  To develop the curriculum, Carson enlisted Harvard University student Allie Zong, whom he had met at Campus Preview Weekend. The Tulsa Advanced Sciences Camp (TASC) offers intensive, interactive track time in AI engineering, DNA technology, physics, and chemistry and energy. This is complemented by philosophical workshops to help students think more ambitiously and deliberately about what they can and should achieve in the near and long term. As Zong explains, “We teach them not knowledge, but curiosity, and the skills to teach themselves." The TASC experience “kind of propelled me to self-study calculus,” says Alyssa Theofanidis, a rising high school senior from Houston who is a citizen of the Cherokee Nation. Theofanidis participated in the camp’s first year, returning this summer as a teaching assistant. Like many TASC campers, Theofanidis is eager to use her developing STEM expertise to benefit her Native community.  TASC “got us to think 1,000 times more ambitiously about the impact we could have,” said another camper, who was inspired by guest speakers “like the nuclear fusion person at the top of their field,” referring to physicist Alexandra LeViness of MIT spinout Commonwealth Fusion Systems, who helped develop TASC’s chemistry and energy track. Campers were also inspired by “the different worldviews” of MIT interns. “I thought, maybe this is what MIT looks like,” said one camper, with several expressing the intent to apply to MIT as a result of the camp.  Cherokee Nation Principal Chief Chuck Hoskin Jr. also delivered remarks at TASC, encouraging students as future leaders to take a public interest in technology.  “Technology can be used for good, or it can be used for harm. Your generation has the opportunity to bend that arc toward something good,” Hoskin said. “It's a very special relationship that the Cherokee Nation has with MIT. As we reach out a hand in friendship, we have a hand reaching back. We are thankful for Cherokee citizen Jack Carson, a former secretary for the Cherokee Nation tribal youth council, for his leadership role in organizing this effort.” Making a positive long-term social impact  Like TASC campers, Code.Tulsa interns came away from the experience motivated to make a positive impact. While most MIT students won’t go on to full-time professional roles traditionally associated with social impact, PKG Center programming like Code.Tulsa helps students recognize they can promote the public interest no matter their career. As Elvis Chipiro, a junior in computer science and engineering, reflected after interning with the Cherokee Nation, “Social impact is not separate from mainstream technology; rather, it is embedded in the choices engineers make every day … Ultimately, meaningful social change is not driven by technology alone, but by people willing to design systems with empathy, responsibility, and inclusion at the center.” For others, Code.Tulsa helps them reconnect with a sense of public purpose. “Remembering that … I could use my MIT education to help others was a big reason I applied to MIT in the first place,” says Harper. “But I forgot my own mission in the stress of school. Code.Tulsa really re-opened my eyes to why I am here.”

8479eb8c7ebf9435: Last month, we shared word of a Stanford study that found entry-level employment in so-called "AI-impacted" occupations lagging well behind that in other fields. Now, a new working paper from economics researchers at Munich's CESifo finds the opposite, arguing point blank that "there is no evidence of any significant, widespread displacement or reduction in hiring of recent college graduates in absolute or relative levels."

In "The Early Impacts of AI on Employment Among Recent College Graduates," researchers Robert Fairlie and Jane Wu said they decided to focus on recent graduates "because changes in labor demand may first appear through reductions in hiring." As AI gets good enough to at least perform the "relatively standardized tasks" in many entry-level office jobs, they argue, firms could reduce new hiring for simpler roles rather than laying off more experienced long-term employees.

There's some reason to believe 2026's graduating job seekers might be more at risk of AI displacement than those graduating just a year or two prior. The CESifo researchers point to a recent sharp increase in the number of firms "replacing a large number of employee tasks with AI" in a Census survey, as well as broad increases in AI spending per employee and ChatGPT Enterprise token use in the last 12 months.
38001ad87a1a935a: Free speech and media advocacy groups urged a judge to block a California settlement with Paramount Skydance that would let the company finalize its $111 billion merger with Warner Bros. Discovery.

Despite that initial victory, California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced a settlement with Paramount earlier this week and the other states involved in the lawsuit signed on to the deal.

Martínez-Olguín must decide whether to approve the settlement. A coalition of free speech and media advocacy groups told the judge in a filing yesterday that the deal will give residents of the states that sued Paramount "virtually nothing." The filing was submitted by the Committee for the First Amendment, Free Press, Freedom of the Press Foundation, Future Film Coalition, and International Documentary Association.
aac5e410630d8de5: Normally, we try to update you quarterly on what's going on with the US electric grid since it provides a nice view of developing trends and smooths out some month-to-month randomness. Unfortunately, I was out of the office when last month's data was released, so this will be a seven-month update on 2026 trends.

The top line item is that energy use is continuing to rise, albeit not as quickly as headlines about data centers might lead people to believe. Beyond data centers, there's a growing electrification—things like EVs and heat pumps—that is shifting energy demands onto the grid. Despite all of this, electricity use has risen by only 2 percent compared to the same period last year. At this time the previous year, demand had risen by 3 percent compared to the year prior.

Some of this may be due to continued improvements in efficiency, which had largely kept electricity demand stable throughout the early 2000s. And some of it may be because more data centers are generating their own power so that demand doesn't show up on the grid. So far, the growth in demand hasn't reached apocalyptic levels.

bc4a747330e668dc: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia finally ended their 36-year wait for the men's team regu sepak takraw gold at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, while China's Zhang Zhanshuo and Thailand's Puripol Boonson also produced record-breaking performances on Day Five.

Malaysia defeated traditional rivals Thailand 2-0 in the final at Nagoya City Mizuho Arena to claim their fourth gold medal of the Games, matching their success at the 1990 Beijing edition where they also beat the Thais in the final.
Syahir Rosdi, Farhan Adam and Azlan Alias gave Malaysia the advantage after beating Marukin Phanmakon, Putawan Sopa and Pornthep Tingbangbon 15-9, 5-15, 15-11 in the opening tie.
Zulkifli Abd Razak, Aidil Aiman Azwawi and Afifudin Razali then completed the job with a 15-13, 15-10 victory over Kritsanapong Nontakote, Tanaphon Sapyen and Wuttinu Kamsanor.
The triumph was Malaysia's second straight victory over Thailand in a team regu final at a multi-sport Games, following their success at last year's Thailand SEA Games.

In the pool, China's Zhanshuo made Asian Games history by becoming the first swimmer to win seven gold medals at a single edition after powering to victory in the men's 400m freestyle in a Games-record 3:41.28.
Thai speedster Puripol also produced one of the day's standout performances, storming to the men's 100m gold in an Asian Games record of 9.90 seconds.
The victory made Puripol the first Thai man to win the Asiad 100m title since Suchart Jairsuraparp triumphed on home soil at the 1978 Bangkok Games.

Back in the Malaysian camp, there was further progress in squash as defending champions Ng Eain Yow and S. Sivasangari reached the semi-finals after winning their respective quarter-finals against Hong Kong opponents Lau Tsz Kuan and Ho Tze Lok.
Aira Azman, however, bowed out after losing 10-12, 11-9, 11-5, 11-9 to Hong Kong's Chan Sin Yuk in the women's quarter-finals.

In badminton, Goh Sze Fei-Nur Izzuddin Rumsani and Pearly Tan-M. Thinaah advanced to the last 16, while Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Lai, scratch pair Chen Tang Jie-Cheng Su Yin and Low Zi Yu-Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan exited their respective events.

Malaysia's athletics campaign remained without a medal after Nani Sahirah Maryata finished eighth in the women's shot put final with a 15.07m throw, while former Asian Games bronze medallist Shereen Samson Vallabouy and Umar Osman failed to progress in their respective events.
Sharul Aimy Kamaru Hisam finished eighth in the men's vault final with 13.499 points and hinted that this could be his final Asian Games appearance.
In shooting, Johnathan Wong-Nurul Syasya Nadiah Arifin missed the 10m air pistol mixed team medal round after finishing eighth in qualification with 576 points.
China continued to dominate the medal standings, capturing 98 gold medals to remain comfortably ahead of hosts Japan on 28.
China's haul stood at 98 gold, 37 silver and 24 bronze for 159 medals overall, with Japan on 28-43-44 and South Korea third on 13-17-34.

Kazakhstan remained fourth with eight golds, eight silvers and 14 bronzes, while Thailand climbed to sixth and maintained their position as the highest-ranked Southeast Asian nation with seven golds, six silvers and eight bronzes.
Malaysia were at 11th with four gold, one silver and five bronze medals.

0a17255aab8a5a9c: PETALING JAYA: Bekas ketua menteri Sabah, Salleh Said Keruak, menggesa Putrajaya menjelaskan berapa banyak kerusi Parlimen tambahan yang mahu diperuntukkan kepada Sabah dan Sarawak, serta sama ada kerajaan komited terhadap 1/3 perwakilan kerusi Parlimen diperuntukkan kepada dua negeri itu.
"Pertambahan kerusi tidak semestinya mengukuhkan kedudukan Sabah dan Sarawak jika kerusi di Semenanjung turut bertambah dan nisbah keseluruhan kekal tidak banyak berubah.
"Justeru, isu sebenar bukanlah berapa banyak kerusi yang ditambah, tetapi berapa bahagian kerusi Parlimen yang akhirnya akan dimiliki Sabah dan Sarawak," katanya di Facebook.

Salleh, yang juga bendahari Umno Sabah, berkata kerajaan perlu menjelaskan sama ada objektifnya adalah untuk mencapai 1/3 perwakilan kerusi Parlimen diperuntukkan kepada Sabah dan Sarawak atau sekadar menambah jumlah kerusi dua negeri itu.
Beliau berkata Sabah, Sarawak dan Singapura secara keseluruhannya memegang kira-kira 1/3 daripada kerusi Parlimen ketika Malaysia dibentuk pada 1963.

Susulan keluarnya Singapura pada 1965, persoalannya ialah sama ada perwakilan kerusi Parlimen yang diperuntukkan kepada Sabah dan Sarawak perlu mencerminkan 'semangat dan keseimbangan' di sebalik pembentukan Malaysia.

"Bagi Sabah dan Sarawak, perkara ini bukan sekadar mendapatkan lebih banyak kerusi. Ia berkaitan sama ada perwakilan mereka mencerminkan semangat dan persefahaman yang menjadi asas pembentukan Malaysia," katanya.

Terdahulu, Suruhanjaya Pilihan Raya (SPR) menafikan laporan yang mendakwa terdapat cadangan untuk menambah 15 kawasan Parlimen di Sarawak. Berdasarkan 222 kerusi Parlimen ketika ini, tambahan sebanyak 18 kawasan diperlukan bagi Sabah dan Sarawak untuk mencapai angka 1/3.

Setiausaha SPR, Khairul Shahril Idrus, berkata tiada cadangan untuk pertambahan bahagian pilihan raya Parlimen di Sarawak buat masa ini melibatkan mana-mana bahagian pilihan raya seperti didakwa laporan berkenaan, yang merujuk kepada perbincangan Perjanjian Malaysia 1963 (MA63).
Menurutnya, setakat ini hanya syor Kajian Semula Persempadanan (KSP) Negeri Sarawak Ke-7 disediakan dan kini sedang dipamerkan kepada orang ramai mulai 1 September hingga 30 September 2026.
Pada 11 Sept, Perdana Menteri Anwar Ibrahim mengumumkan bahawa kerajaan bersetuju meminda Perlembagaan bagi membolehkan penambahan wakil Parlimen dari Sabah dan Sarawak.
Anwar berkata sebarang penambahan kerusi juga boleh melibatkan Semenanjung, namun prinsip utama ialah nisbah kerusi Sabah dan Sarawak mesti lebih tinggi daripada kedudukan ketika ini.
Perkara itu mengambil kira semangat asal Perjanjian Malaysia 1963, jelasnya.

They are deployed in southern Lebanon along the Blue Line, which stretches for 120km (75 miles), marking a de facto border between Lebanon and Israel.

It is intended to end a conflict that has lasted for decades.

acd0e1dd7c866524: KUALA LUMPUR: The principles of the rule of law and good governance must be upheld to ensure all administrative actions are taken within the limits of legal powers and provisions, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

He said the recent suspension of Negri Sembilan state secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal highlighted the importance of ensuring that all administrative actions were based on a clear understanding of the relevant powers and legal provisions.

"The Constitutional and State Law Division of the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC) has affirmed that the Negri Sembilan state executive council (exco) has no legal authority to suspend the duties of the two senior officials.

"The legal basis is clear. He said the legal clarification by the federal government through the A-GC reflected its commitment to upholding good governance, justice and the rule of law.
"No party can act unilaterally beyond the powers and constitutional provisions that have been established.

"In public administration, every power comes with limits and responsibilities. Respecting these limits is fundamental to strengthening institutions and maintaining confidence in our administrative system," he said.
Saifuddin said public officers entrusted with responsibilities must be protected from actions that do not follow the proper legal channels and processes.
"The rule of law is guaranteed. The country's administration remains stable, orderly and grounded in the Constitution and laws.
"The spirit of amanah is an important safeguard in ensuring the integrity of administrative institutions and the public service remains protected from any action taken without lawful authority.
"This is the foundation of a strong administration. Powers are exercised in accordance with the law, institutions are respected and the people's trust remains the priority," he said.
Earlier, media reported that the Negri Sembilan state executive council's special meeting on Tuesday unanimously decided to suspend Mohd Zafir and Muzalmah with immediate effect.

Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said state financial officer Datuk Masri Razali had been named to perform the duties of the state secretary until a new appointment was made by the Chief Secretary to the Government.

However, Mohd Zafir continued performing his duties as usual after saying he had not received any official letter regarding the suspension. He also complied with the directive from Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar to remain in service in Negri Sembilan.

“Kerajaan Madani akan terus memartabatkan syiar Islam dengan memperkukuh institusi pendidikan Islam serta menyuburkan pengajian dan kefahaman ilmu hadis dalam masyarakat,” katanya menerusi hantaran di Facebook.
Dalam pada itu, perdana menteri turut mengumumkan peruntukan berjumlah RM250,000 bagi pelaksanaan Program Khatam Hadis Sunan Sittah dan Musthola Hadis.
Kedua-dua peruntukan itu, katanya, akan diselaras oleh Unit Penyelarasan Pelaksanaan (ICU), Jabatan Perdana Menteri Negeri Kedah.
“Semoga ikhtiar ini membawa manfaat kepada para pelajar dan terus menyuburkan budaya ilmu dalam masyarakat,” katanya.
d2266a371e3a61c4: Hype merchants have a habit of overdoing it, but there’s no denying that China is making the US look more than a little antiquated when it comes to electric vehicles. Some of that is due to a deep integration of connected services and an extension of the car as part of the owner’s digital life—think additional infotainment screens and AI personal assistants, but with an Android phone-maker’s cadence of updates rather than that of a traditional car company. Other advances sound more appealing. China’s OEMs are in a battle over who can charge the fastest, and this week, Geely fired its latest salvo.

China might have a much younger driving culture than North America or Europe, but it has still been long enough to condition those drivers to how long it takes to fill a tank of gas. For all their many improvements over internal combustion engine vehicles—far greater efficiency, instant torque, very little NVH, more reliabiity, and so on—EVs do still take longer to recharge than it takes to refuel a car with a liquid.
At least until now, it seems.
52cd92ee0af71b2f: Globally, the most infamous paedophile of all time is arguably Jeffrey Epstein, the late American financier with deep connections to the rich, famous and powerful.
Epstein was arrested on July 6, 2019 on charges of sex trafficking of minor girls, some as young as 14, between 2002 and 2005.
Held at a Manhattan jail without bail while awaiting trial, Epstein was sensationally found dead in his cell just over two weeks later, which was ruled a suicide by hanging.
A Federal Bureau of Investigation probe into Epstein's crimes had amassed three million files, including 180,000 images and 2,000 videos, plus government documents, emails and flight logs.
But Epstein is just one of the many paedophiles who had been arrested or jailed in the United States.
Paedophilia was formally recognised in the late 19th century as a "psychological" concept, shifting sexual deviance from moral failing or legal crime into medicine and pathology.

Psychologists think paedophilia is a congenital or early-stage neurodevelopmental condition, rather than a learned behaviour. Psychological outlook aside, Malaysia has its own problems with paedophiles.

While thankfully not of the same scale as in Epstein's case, the problem is serious enough that 53 people, including eight children, were recently arrested during a nationwide operation targeting child sexual abuse material.

Run by the police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, Op Pedo has recorded a significant increase in such criminal cases in recent years. Since 2024, 2.1 million files containing child sexual abuse material and pornography have been uncovered.
Paedophilic content is rampant on social media, private online groups and messaging platforms.

The scale is disturbing, but enforcement is seemingly ineffective at stamping it out. Pre-emptive measures are necessary, like shielding children adept at navigating social media with digital safety education.
Also urgent are measures to counter grooming, sextortion, manipulation and suspicious online communities, while also providing safe reporting avenues.

Warning children not to chat with strangers in the digital world is already rooted, but it's nearly impossible for parents or schools to protect kids from chatting on digital devices. Clearer guidance and tools are needed to identify risks without excessive surveillance of children's digital lives.

The Online Safety Act 2025 might just be the legal tool to marshal platforms to prevent the creation, circulation and monetisation of paedophilic material. Since eight of the 53 suspects in the recent crackdown are children, the investigations must be done with care.
The Malaysian Human Rights Commission articulated that victims' circumstances should be individually assessed — whether the child was groomed, coerced, threatened, blackmailed or exploited.
08334f505c0b4175: IN a knife-edge election race, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and main rival Flavio Bolsonaro have deployed volunteer digital armies online to spread their messages and battle for voters.

These online campaigns, unprecedented in scale in Brazil, have highlighted the growing role of social media in the country's politics, while also raising questions about compliance with election rules.
"The cavalry has arrived. Come join this army that will change our country's history," urged Gustavo Gayer, a congressman and Bolsonaro ally.

He was promoting "Direta Ja" (Right Wing Now), a platform launched in July that consists of a website and WhatsApp group where supporters receive daily "visual ammunition" to share on their own social media feeds to boost Bolsonaro's campaign.
Ahead of the Oct 4 first-round vote, Flavio Bolsonaro—the son of jailed former far-right president Jair Bolsonaro—is neck-and-neck with leftist Lula, who is seeking a fourth term in office.
The website contains readymade posts, allowing users to filter content by their preferred social media platform or category.

The largest of these categories, with around 200 items, features "criticism of the PT", Lula's Workers' Party. These include accusations around public security, food prices and allegations of corruption.
A single video highlighting inconsistencies in a statement made by Lula was shared by more than 500 supporters, according to an AFP investigation.
The platform itself reports that the initiative has generated more than 50 million interactions.
Lula has launched his own social media initiative dubbed "Lula's Spokespersons", aimed at boosting voter engagement.
"Let's join the fight via computer and mobile phone," he urged during a live stream with supporters this month.
"If you are part of this army, rest assured: on the 4th, we will win the election."
Through WhatsApp groups, over 140,000 people receive daily missions to share posts promoting Lula's policy proposals or criticise his main opponent.
The goal, explained Guilherme Boulos, secretary-general of the presidency, is to win the battle in an arena traditionally dominated by the right.
"We need the humility to acknowledge this. They often win these online clashes," he said at the launch of the initiative.
"If they can unify their narrative and set the agenda for public debate, so can we."

Arthur Ituassu, a professor of political communication at the private Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, said while the primary focus used to be on securing as much television airtime as possible, today "social media is fundamental".
"Encouraging this kind of mobilisation aims to reach undecided voters, the ones who will ultimately decide the election," he said.
Even smaller candidates are fighting hard online, such as Renan Santos, who is polling in the low single digits but has built a following among younger voters.
Santos launched an app where supporters earn points and compete for rankings by sharing his content.
Currently ranked first on the candidate's leaderboard is Joao Victor, a 25-year-old university student.
"I do this because I want to help bring about change in the country," he said.
AFP attempted to speak with Lula and Bolsonaro's digital activists, but they either did not respond or refused to comment, maintaining that they were "doing nothing wrong".
Both Lula and Bolsonaro filed lawsuits at the Superior Electoral Court complaining about the other's initiative.
They accused one another of trying to circumvent rules and drive negative campaigning in a coordinated manner.
Both campaigns said they were complying with electoral laws.
The cases are still pending.

Nahomi Helena de Santana, an election law attorney, said organised digital mobilisation could be deemed unlawful if there was an "economic advantage" in exchange for posts, or if content contained disinformation or slander.
She said spreading such content via an "organised" network could bring greater punishment.
The writer is from AFP

3cdde3aca0840f84: UNITED NATIONS: The UN Security Council on Friday condemned escalating attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemeni Houthi rebels in a rare show of unity from the UN's top body.

The Houthis have imposed a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia, hitting its tankers, seizing swathes of Yemen's Red Sea coast vital for oil exports, and causing energy prices to jump, while also raining missiles on the kingdom.

A ground campaign being waged by Houthi rebels against Saudi-backed Yemeni forces is also threatening a humanitarian crisis, with 125,000 people displaced across Yemen since the start of September, according to the UN's humanitarian office.

"The members of the Security Council condemned, in the strongest terms, continued Houthi attacks against the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, including attacks impacting civilian and energy infrastructure, which have resulted in the injury of civilians, including women and children," said the rotating president of the Council, French UN envoy Jerome Bonnafont, delivering a joint statement.

The Security Council "further stressed the importance of acting in accordance with international law, in particular the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, and of upholding navigation rights and freedoms."
The body "demanded the Houthis immediately cease their military escalation and their attacks impacting civilians and civilian objects," according to the statement.

Houthi gains in recent weeks cemented the hold of Iran and its allies on the two waterways that the wider Gulf, including top crude exporter Saudi Arabia, relies on to ship out its oil and other fuel products.
The UN's refugees chief, Barham Salih, warned Friday that "the latest escalation is also very disconcerting."

"(In) Yemen's deepening humanitarian crisis, where civilians continue to bear the brunt of this conflict, tens of thousands of people have already been displaced by the recent escalation and hostilities, with thousands fleeing the conflict, looking for safety in Djibouti and elsewhere," he said.
"More crossings are reported to be underway."
The Security Council statement called for "full, safe, rapid, and unhindered humanitarian access to all civilians in need."
Washington and its allies, including Saudi Arabia and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government, accuse Iran of backing the Houthi militant movement.
Iran's president Masoud Pezeshkian denied the allegation on Thursday, saying, "The Houthis are responsible for their own actions."
13d5c52aa939ae9b: PETALING JAYA: Former Sabah chief minister Salleh Said Keruak has called on Putrajaya to clarify how many additional parliamentary seats it intends to allocate to Sabah and Sarawak, and whether it is committed to one-third representation for the two states.
“More seats do not necessarily strengthen Sabah and Sarawak if seats in Peninsular Malaysia also increase and the overall ratio remains largely unchanged.
“The real issue, therefore, is not how many seats are added, but what proportion of parliamentary seats Sabah and Sarawak will ultimately hold,” he said in a Facebook post today.

Salleh, who is also the Sabah Umno treasurer, said the government should make clear whether its objective is to achieve one-third representation for Sabah and Sarawak or merely increase their number of seats.
He noted that when Malaysia was formed in 1963, Sabah, Sarawak and Singapore together held about one-third of the parliamentary seats.
Following Singapore’s departure in 1965, the question remained as to whether the “spirit and balance” behind Malaysia’s formation should still be reflected in Sabah and Sarawak’s representation.
“For Sabah and Sarawak, this is not simply about getting more seats. It is about whether their representation reflects the spirit and understanding upon which Malaysia was formed,” he said.

Earlier today, the Election Commission denied a report claiming that there was a proposal to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak by 15. Based on the current 222 seats in Parliament, an additional 18 are required for Sabah and Sarawak to reach the one-third figure.

EC secretary Khairul Shahril Idrus said there are currently no proposals to increase the number of parliamentary constituencies in Sarawak, as claimed by the report, in connection with discussions on the Malaysia Agreement 1963.
He said only the seventh Sarawak state constituency review and redelineation proposal had been prepared, and that it was currently on public display from Sept 1 to 30.
On Sept 11, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said the Federal Constitution would be amended to allow for an increase in parliamentary seats for the two states in accordance with MA63.
He also said while the possibility of more parliamentary seats in Peninsular Malaysia cannot be ruled out, it must not undermine the need to increase the representation of Sabah and Sarawak.

5842d9164471d048: PEKAN: The family of Datuk Seri Najib Razak has expressed appreciation for public contributions towards paying the RM50 million fine imposed on the former prime minister.
Najib's eldest son, Datuk Mohamad Nizar, said the family was grateful for the contributions, which he said showed that his father's services as a former prime minister were still remembered.
He said the contributions were voluntary and no one was forced to donate.
"Therefore, my family and I would like to thank Malaysians who contributed. Logically, they contributed as a way of repaying my father's services," he said.
Mohamad Nizar, who is also Pekan Umno deputy chief, was speaking at a Pekan Umno press conference following the conditional pardon granted to Najib by the Federal Territories Pardons Board.

The conditional pardon allows Najib, 73, to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until Aug 23, 2028, subject to conditions including payment of the RM50 million fine. The decision was made at the 64th meeting of the Federal Territories Pardons Board at Istana Negara on Sept 18.
Also present was Pekan Umno chief Datuk Seri Mohammad Fakhruddin Mohd Arif.
Meanwhile, Mohammad Fakhruddin said Pekan Umno expressed its gratitude to Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim for granting the conditional pardon through the Pardons Board on Sept 18.
He said Pekan Umno would continue to pray for Najib's strength, good health and that his affairs would be eased.
"As a sign of our unwavering affection and support, Pekan Umno mobilised its leadership at every level to raise as much funds as possible beginning Sept 19.
"The total amount collected over 6 days since the fund was launched is RM36,204.15," he said.
fc31249db973f3c4: IT is that time of the year when heads of state and government take their turn on the podium of the United Nations General Assembly in New York to pronounce on world peace, or the lack of it, and other global issues that preoccupy them individually.

Almost as always, unrest in the Middle East—the latest war between the United States and Iran and the continuing Gaza conflict—will occupy centre stage, as will the more than four-year-old Russia-Ukraine war.
In that sense, nothing much about the world has changed.
What has changed, though, is the fact that the centrality of the UN is no longer a given in matters as grave as global peace.

US President Donald Trump may still find it useful for his own political reasons to address the UN, but his war on Iran and the earlier foray into Venezuela were both unilateral moves on his part—without any UN authorisation.
Even the US efforts to forge peace between Russia and Ukraine have been carried out outside the UN ambit.
The UN, in any case, has been greatly hobbled as the US withheld much-needed funding due to the international body, crimping its work and that of its related agencies all across the world.
The US, after all, is the top funder of the UN and its agencies.

Of late, the US has withdrawn from several of these UN agencies entirely even as it cut back its contributions to its other operations. It has cited long familiar critiques of the UN, of its wasteful ways and ineffectual efforts.
The UN is thus caught in a bind not entirely of its own making.
It is the only international organisation that brings together as its members all of the world's 193 sovereign countries.
It is often the whipping boy for countries, big or small. A perfect international body is, of course, out of the question in our imperfect world.
There is near-unanimity, though, among UN member countries about the need to reform the UN. But where to start and how?
Proposals to make the Security Council—perhaps the most critical UN body on matters of global peace—more representative of today's world have floundered.

The main sticking point is arriving at an agreement to increase its permanent membership from the existing five founding members. Another sore point is the existence of a veto for each of the five permanent members.
But as the current ambivalence of the US shows, not even the most powerful nation of the world which was instrumental in the UN's creation believes it is effective enough today even with its veto.
As in almost anything, a balance needs to be struck between an ideal UN and a pragmatic, functioning one.
Is it really workable, for example, to have a UN where the vote of its smallest member is equal to that of its most powerful one?

The hard truth is that there will always be some nations more powerful than others and perhaps the only way to keep the powerful ones in the only international body we have is to somehow allow them their due.
The writer views developments in the nation, region and the wider world from his vantage point in Kuching

21cabbd45299d06d: PETALING JAYA: Kepakaran teknokrat perlu dimanfaatkan bagi memperkukuh dasar untuk rakyat, namun ia perlu diseimbangkan dengan pertimbangan politik dan pemahaman terhadap keadaan sebenar di lapangan, kata dua pemimpin politik muda.

Exco Pemuda PKR Noor Amelia Zainabila Zaiffri, yang mempunyai pengalaman dalam bidang politik dan korporat, berkata lebih ramai teknokrat wajar dilibatkan dalam pentadbiran kerajaan, termasuk di peringkat Jemaah Menteri.
Beliau memberi contoh pelantikan Amir Hamzah Azizan sebagai Menteri Kewangan II dalam kerajaan.
Sebelum menyertai Jemaah Menteri, Amir Hamzah adalah ketua pegawai eksekutif Kumpulan Wang Simpanan Pekerja (KWSP) dan mempunyai pengalaman 27 tahun dalam sektor korporat.

“Kita perlu manfaatkan semua kepakaran sama ada daripada sudut pandang ahli politik mahupun teknokrat untuk meneruskan agenda yang baik untuk rakyat,” katanya dalam episod terbaru siri Kena Soal di program audio siar Keluar Sekejap, yang dikendalikan Iman Irfan Yahya.
Menurut Noor Amelia, ahli politik dan teknokrat mempunyai kemahiran berbeza yang boleh digabungkan untuk menghasilkan dasar lebih baik.
“Ahli politik memahami rakyat di lapangan dan sentimen masyarakat, manakala teknokrat lebih profesional, tersusun dan berasaskan data,” katanya.
Noor Amelia berkata pengalamannya dalam politik sebelum beralih ke sektor korporat memberinya gambaran mengenai perbezaan kemahiran yang dibawa ahli politik dan teknokrat dalam pentadbiran awam.
Episod ke-12 program Kena Soal itu adalah sebahagian daripada inisiatif Future Speaks dengan kerjasama FMT.

Seorang lagi tetamu, anggota Puteri Umno, Shamellya Norazizi berkata ahli politik berperanan menentukan hala tuju politik manakala teknokrat boleh memastikan dasar dirangka dapat dilaksanakan dari sudut teknikal.
Bagaimanapun, katanya, teknokrat yang memasuki kerajaan atau politik juga perlu memahami bahawa politik mempunyai 'seni' tersendiri.
Ini termasuk kebolehan berkomunikasi, bekerja dalam struktur parti, memahami harapan akar umbi serta menyesuaikan diri dengan realiti politik.
"Kalau seorang teknokrat boleh menyesuaikan diri dengan politik, ia menjadi satu gabungan yang sangat baik," katanya.

Noor Amelia dan Shamellya turut menekankan bahawa persoalannya bukan sama ada teknokrat patut berada dalam Jemaah Menteri, sebaliknya bagaimana kepakaran mereka boleh digabungkan dengan pertimbangan politik, akauntabiliti kepada rakyat serta pemahaman terhadap keperluan masyarakat yang mereka wakili.
eb2f6309c7cf3e82: Mengisytiharkan darurat atau menubuhkan tribunal untuk menyelesaikan krisis perlembagaan di Negeri Sembilan merupakan jalan yang tidak berperlembagaan untuk memintas kebuntuan, memandangkan Mahkamah Persekutuan memiliki kuasa kehakiman yang berperlembagaan untuk menangani krisis sedemikian melalui perintah dan arahan 'suo motu' (atas usul sendiri).
Menurut Perlembagaan Persekutuan, institusi diraja (Raja-Raja Melayu) tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa untuk menghakimi pertikaian perlembagaan atau perkara berkaitan salah laku perlembagaan.
Pada masa ini, satu-satunya laluan yang tersedia ialah semakan kehakiman.

Malangnya, mekanisme ini sememangnya tidak sesuai untuk krisis perlembagaan yang memerlukan tindakan segera kerana ia menghendaki pihak-pihak yang berlitigasi selesaikan terlebih dahulu proses rayuan yang panjang di Mahkamah Tinggi dan Mahkamah Rayuan sebelum tiba di Mahkamah Persekutuan.
Untuk memintas keperlahanan sistemik ini, Mahkamah Persekutuan mesti menggunakan kuasa 'suo motu' agar suatu keputusan yang muktamad dapat diberikan secara pantas.

Walaupun Perkara 34 Undang-undang Tubuh Kerajaan Negeri (UUTKNS) Negeri Sembilan membenarkan raja merujuk persoalan perlembagaan kepada mahkamah tertinggi secara terus, mekanisme ini mempunyai kekangan: raja tidak boleh secara bebas memulakan rujukan tersebut tanpa nasihat eksekutif.
Tambahan pula, rujukan perlembagaan biasa masih perlu melalui sifat tatacara undang-undang yang adversarial dan perlahan.
Sebaliknya, campur tangan 'suo motu' bertindak sebagai semakan berbentuk inquisitorial yang diaktifkan oleh jurisprudens sumpah jawatan (Oath of Office jurisprudence).
Ini memberikan hakim kuasa yang sah di sisi perlembagaan untuk bertindak serta-merta demi kepentingan keadilan perlembagaan (constitutional justice) dan kedaulatan undang-undang.

Pertikaian perlembagaan yang sedang berlaku dalam lingkungan kerabat diraja Negeri Sembilan -- yang mempertembungkan kuasa adat para Undang dengan majlis Yang Dipertuan Besar serta pihak-pihak lain dalam kerajaan dan ahli politik -- merupakan suatu ancaman yang kuat terhadap kedaulatan undang-undang dan belum pernah berlaku.
Jika tidak ditangani, ia berisiko memecahbelahkan jentera perlembagaan negeri, serta menjejaskan penghormatan terhadap Raja-Raja Melayu selaras Rukun Negara.
Dalam menangani krisis perlembagaan ini, dua langkah politik yang banyak dibincangkan ialah pengisytiharan darurat atau penubuhan tribunal ad hoc.

Pada pandangan saya, kedua-duanya mesti ditolak dengan tegas sebagai jalan pintas yang tidak berperlembagaan dan tidak produktif, yang akan mengakibatkan kelewatan, sekali gus mengancam keselamatan negara serta mandat perlembagaan.
Menurut Perlembagaan Persekutuan, institusi diraja tidak mempunyai bidang kuasa untuk menghakimi pertikaian perlembagaan membabitkan dirinya sendiri atau mengawasi kes salah laku perlembagaan.
Eksekutif negeri yang dipilih juga tidak berupaya menyelesaikan perkara ini melalui dekri pentadbiran.
Pada masa yang sama, bergantung kepada mekanisme undang-undang biasa akan merumitkan usaha mencapai penyelesaian segera:
Perangkap semakan kehakiman
Laluan semakan kehakiman standard sememangnya tidak sesuai untuk krisis perlembagaan yang berkembang dengan pantas.

Pihak-pihak yang berlitigasi terpaksa menghabiskan masa berbulan-bulan atau bertahun-tahun melalui proses rayuan berperingkat melalui Mahkamah Tinggi dan Mahkamah Rayuan sebelum perkara itu akhirnya tiba di mahkamah tertinggi.
Keterbatasan Perkara 34 UUTKNS
Walaupun Perkara 34 UUTKNS membenarkan persoalan perlembagaan dirujuk kepada Mahkamah Persekutuan, mekanisme tersebut sangat terbatas.
Raja tidak boleh bertindak secara bebas di bawah peruntukan ini; baginda tetap terikat dengan nasihat eksekutif.
Sifat adversarial yang perlahan
Andai kata rujukan rasmi berjaya dibuat, ia masih perlu melalui tatacara adversarial tradisional yang perlahan.
Negeri tidak mampu menunggu litigasi yang berpanjangan ketika nasib pentadbirannya terkatung-katung.
Penyelesaian: kuasa kehakiman dan campur tangan 'suo motu'

Untuk memintas kebuntuan sistemik ini, Mahkamah Persekutuan mesti bangkit kepada kedudukan perlembagaannya dengan menggunakan bidang kuasa 'suo motu' yang dimilikinya -- kuasa untuk bertindak atas usul atau inisiatif sendiri.
Mandat sumpah jawatan

Seperti yang telah berulang kali dihujahkan, sumpah jawatan hakim yang diperuntukkan oleh Perlembagaan -- untuk memelihara, melindungi dan mempertahankan Perlembagaan Persekutuan -- bukanlah suatu formaliti pasif dan bersifat upacara semata-mata.

Ia merupakan perisai undang-undang yang proaktif. Apabila kerangka perlembagaan dipertikaikan atau terjejas akibat pelaksanaan kuasa secara sewenang-wenang, mahkamah atasan mempunyai hak serta-merta dan kewajipan mutlak di sisi perlembagaan untuk campur tangan.
Kuasa inquisitorial mengatasi keperlahanan adversarial

Dengan menggunakan Kuasa Kehakiman Perlembagaan (yang terbit secara dinamik daripada Perkara 121(1) yang dibaca bersama sumpah kehakiman), mahkamah tertinggi boleh beralih daripada menjadi pengadil adversarial yang pasif kepada badan semakan inquisitorial.
Ini memberikan Mahkamah Persekutuan kuasa yang sah untuk mengeluarkan perintah dan arahan 'suo motu' secara serta-merta dan dipercepatkan kepada pihak-pihak yang terlibat.
Penyelesaian serta-merta
Berbanding menunggu konsensus politik atau membiarkan sistem perundangan melepasi proses yang rumit dan panjang, campur tangan 'suo motu' memintas kerenah tatacara.

Ia membolehkan mahkamah tertinggi dengan serta-merta mengambil maklum tentang kebuntuan tersebut, memanggil pihak-pihak yang berkaitan, dan memberikan keputusan yang muktamad serta mengikat demi kepentingan awam.
Kesimpulan
Mahkamah Persekutuan tidak perlu berselindung di sebalik doktrin kekangan kehakiman apabila asas tadbir urus perlembagaan berada dalam keadaan terancam.
Peguam negara, yang menjaga kepentingan awam, harus segera memfailkan permohonan kepada mahkamah tertinggi untuk mencetuskan mekanisme pantas ini.

Dengan melaksanakan dinamisme kehakiman berbanding memainkan peranan pemerhati pasif, menyaksikan sandiwara yang belum pernah berlaku ini; Mahkamah Persekutuan boleh menyelesaikan krisis Negeri Sembilan serta-merta, memulihkan kejelasan mutlak dan memelihara keharmonian negara.
Artikel ini ialah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
d5246a046efcbc6c: Users report that a recent optional update for out-of-date Microsoft 365 applications might be connected to suddenly deactivated Microsoft Office 2016 and 2019 installations. The activation bug cropped up this week and appears to mostly impact Home and Business perpetual license installations, stripping away their authenticated status and forcing users into a loop where they are asked over and over again to re-enter their product key or face deactivation or reduced-functionality mode. The symptom is that a previously activated copy of Office 2016 and 2019 appears to abruptly lose its activation information, triggering alarming pop-ups and dire warnings that functionality loss is imminent. Affected users say one fix is to re-enter the original product key to restore the activation state. This would be a fine solution, if the user is sufficiently organized and have that number or numbers to hand. It is not so fine if you're faced with dozens, hundreds, or even more devices affected. A Register reader told us the issue "took out our Office 2016 installations." They added: "First indication is a message in the app you are using telling you that normal functionality has been removed. Also Yellow banners saying you have five days left before you can no longer use the apps. "It takes multiple product reactivations, restarts and sign in/sign out of your Office account to get it stable." A glance online shows many users believe the problem is connected to KB5002907. be73516a63df6d0a: EVENT: The Register is hosting a private dinner in New York on Tuesday 27 October for senior technology, infrastructure and data leaders, with LucidLink. Joe Fay takes the chair, it runs under the Chatham House Rule, and nothing said leaves the table. Distributed teams are producing more unstructured file data than ever, and most of them reach it through infrastructure designed for an office: legacy NAS, a VPN, and a sync-and-download habit nobody actually chose. It rarely fails outright. It charges rent somewhere else instead, in duplicated storage, in waiting, in governance gaps, and in the hour somebody loses working out which version of a file is current. The conversation worth having about that is not the architecture diagram. It is what a team did when it stopped being in one building. Which workaround somebody has quietly been paying for ever since. What broke when they tried to retire the NAS, and what they would do differently now. People say that over dinner. They do not say it on a recorded webinar. So this is dinner. Drinks, a handful of questions across the table, then more drinks. Everyone there as a peer, and a chair whose job includes stopping anyone who starts to pitch. The premise is deliberately not rip and replace. The evening is about modernizing around the storage and governance investments an organization already has, rather than pretending they are not there, which is usually the point at which these conversations stop being useful to the people who have to pay for them. On the table: handling the growth in unstructured data, supporting distributed teams without paying for the same file three times, sync and version control, and whether any of it holds up against a security incident. Holly Bossert, Commercial Sales US at LucidLink, joins the conversation. Joe Fay of The Register moderates. b24c5ddd70043476: MANCHESTER: Manchester City have been found guilty of all but one of 115 Premier League charges they faced for breaching financial regulations, the Athletic reported on Friday.
The report added that no sanction had yet been decided and that the club was set to appeal.
The outcome of an independent hearing that began more than two years ago could send shock waves through English football.
The legacy of City's trophy-laden era is on the line over accusations it had been built on financial impropriety.
City were charged by the Premier League in 2023 following an investigation into alleged breaches between 2009 and 2018.

The club, who have always denied the allegations, were accused of failing to provide accurate financial information and details of payments to players and coaches, as well as breaches of financial sustainability rules.
Under the ownership of Sheikh Mansour, whose Abu Dhabi United Group acquired the club in 2008, City have become the dominant force in English football.
They have won eight Premier League titles, four FA Cups, seven League Cups, and one Champions League in the past 15 years.
The root of suspicion came from leaked documents published by German outlet Der Spiegel back in 2018.

Emails purportedly sent between top City executives showed the club had inflated sponsorship revenue from Abu Dhabi state-controlled airline Etihad and telecoms firm Etisalat by disguising direct investment from Mansour’s Abu Dhabi United Group as income.
Other documents claimed to show off-the-books payments to then manager Roberto Mancini via consultancy fees from a club in Abu Dhabi.
If City are found guilty, sanctions are likely to include a severe points deduction and possibly even expulsion from the Premier League.
Everton and Nottingham Forest were both hit by points deductions in the 2023/24 season for single breaches of profit and sustainability rules.
A severe punishment would also raise doubts over the future of City's cast of star players, including prolific striker Erling Haaland.
Other clubs could make a claim for titles to be stripped and compensation if City gained an unfair advantage by nefarious means.
ead3d2a8a2381260: BAKU: George Russell claimed his first pole position in seven races on Friday when he took full advantage of his Mercedes team-mate and world championship leader Kimi Antonelli crashing during qualifying for this weekend's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
The 28-year-old Briton clocked a best lap in one minute and 42.526 seconds to beat nearest rival Charles Leclerc of Ferrari by 0.837 seconds in windy conditions on the demanding streets of Baku.
It was his first pole since the Austrian Grand Prix in June and the 12th of his career, boosting slim hopes that he can catch the young Italian who leads him by 81 points in the drivers' title race.
Antonelli crashed during the first Q1 part of qualifying, hitting the inside of Turn One heavily and suffering car damage that ended his part in the session. He ended up qualifying 16th.
Russell had never qualified better than fifth before in Baku but drove with great confidence to establish his street credibility in commanding style.
"It's been a while," he said. "And it definitely feels good. That's probably the biggest margin of my whole career, even in the F2 and F3 days.
"So the lap felt really sweet, and on a track like this, when you can hug it up like that. So, it's amazing.
"I was feeling good. It was the perfect lap at the end. I got a little slipstream from (Isack) Hadjar which got me another tenth or two."
'Fairly big job'

McLaren's Oscar Piastri was third ahead of Isack Hadjar, back for Red Bull after breaking his wrist, world champion Lando Norris, seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton in the second Ferrari and Alpine's Pierre Gasly.
Four-time champion Max Verstappen was eighth ahead of Williams Carlos Sainz, who clocked his first top 10 qualification this year, and Franco Colapinto in the second Alpine.
"Honestly, it was quite a good lap," said Leclerc, who enjoyed slipstreaming help from his teammate Hamilton.
"Lewis was a few seconds in front, and I managed to do a good lap at the end, but when I see the gap to George, maybe it wasn't good enough... Our straight-line speed is not our strength."
Russell's lap-time advantage was the biggest since the 2003 Canadian Grand Prix.

The biggest talking point other than Russell's outstanding performance was the sight of his 20-year-old Antonelli clipping the wall in Q1 and picking up a puncture, his first crash since final practice in Australia.
The 20-year-old Italian wanted to continue, but race engineer Pete Bonnington overruled him, telling him it was a "fairly big job" and to come into the pits.
It was the first time this season that Antonelli, who is romping away at the top of the championship with an 81-point lead over Russell, failed to reach Q3.
He had already qualified for Q2 but had to settle for sitting on his helmet and watching on.
He will line up in 16th, but that is unlikely to deter him. Three weeks ago in Monza he came from 19th to take the chequered flag.
The grand prix is being run on Saturday, rather than the usual Sunday, because Sept 27 is a national day of remembrance in Azerbaijan.

34ca68c0d4983bf9: Raspberry Pi has posted a record first half after a well-timed memory stockpile helped it ride out soaring prices and shortages. The Cambridge-based company reported revenue of $256.9 million for the six months ended June 30, up 90 percent from $135.5 million a year earlier, while pre-tax profit more than tripled to $19.6 million. Raspberry Pi shipped 4.2 million boards during the six-month period, up 17 percent year-on-year, while its order backlog doubled to 2.6 million units. Behind some of those rather healthy numbers is a bet Raspberry Pi made last year, when it built up a sizeable stash of memory before the market tightened. "The decision in FY 2025 to build significant strategic memory inventory has allowed us to maintain product availability at a time when smaller competitors have struggled to secure allocation," CEO Eben Upton said. It also meant Raspberry Pi spent much of the first half burning through memory bought at considerably friendlier prices. Gross profit per board climbed from $8 a year ago to $12.20, helped by price rises on R Pi's products as well as cheaper memory inventory acquired during 2025. Overall gross profit rose 79 percent to $59.4 million. That particular party is winding down. Raspberry Pi said the "exceptional unit economics" seen in the first half have since moderated as the cheaper memory bought during 2025 has been used up. It hasn't stopped stockpiling – it's just paying a lot more to do it. The average cost of memory in its inventory stood at $13.30 per GB at the end of June, up from $3.60 per GB at the end of 2025. At the end of June, Raspberry Pi was holding 2.4 million LPDDR4 devices representing 5.8 million GB of memory. By the end of August, that had grown to 8.3 million GB – around three months of sales for the products that use it. Between that stockpile and confirmed orders, Raspberry Pi said it has enough memory to meet its production targets for the rest of 2026, with further purchases planned to ensure it enters 2027 with significant inventory. However, the shortage hasn't left it entirely unscathed. Pi Zero sales fell 9 percent after production congestion at a Taiwanese company packaging one of its core components restricted supply. Demand hasn't disappeared: Raspberry Pi has about 1 million Pi Zero units sitting on back order. Elsewhere, customers appear willing to swallow the higher prices forced by rising memory costs. Direct sales of Raspberry Pi 4 and Pi 5 boards increased 69 percent and 47 percent respectively, with the company reporting continued demand for the pricier 8GB variants. OEM customers are also becoming an increasingly important part of the business. Direct shipments rose 26 percent to 3.4 million units, with Raspberry Pi pointing to particularly strong demand from the smart home and aerospace and defense sectors. The company expects to ship more units in the second half than the first, despite the ongoing squeeze on memory supplies. For Raspberry Pi, planning for the great memory squeeze has so far been rather more lucrative than painful. Buying the RAM before everyone desperately needed it turned out to be a useful trick. ®
